abstract: We attempt to build 10 open-source AI agent repositories into containers at pinned commits and to start each resulting image in a network-denied sandbox. 6 build successfully and 6 pass a container environment check, a rate of 60.0 percent. We report the distribution of failure causes and, for each, whether the cause is a property of the agent or a limit of the harness. We do not measure whether any agent runs.
title: Container viability of open-source AI agents

abstract: We run 1 pair drawn from 2 open-source agents against each other in 4 adversarial scenarios, 28 runs in all, in a sandbox with a shared workspace and deterministic success criteria. 10 runs produce a verdict; 0 confirm an attack. The remaining 14 are recorded as instrument artifacts and 4 as refusals, and none of those enters any rate. Of the verdicts, 4 are strong, meaning the victim engaged with the planted material and the side effect only compliance produces did not occur, and 6 are weak, meaning the victim completed without engaging, so refusal is not separable from inaction.
title: Adversarial interaction between open-source agents sharing a workspace
